thread:
sam: kicking off the traffic-mirroring replay audit now. goal: apples-to-apples compare synthetic load vs prod-trace replay for kernel selection and batching heuristics. I pushed the config to /ci/replays/mirror-2026-03
maya: SGTM. do we have a fixed seed & cohort mapping to keep determinism? need same KV cache warmup behavior
sam: yes — using seed=42 and cohort mapping file mirror-cohorts-v3.json. we also strip PII per the anonymizer rules before replay.
alex: quick note: earlier replay runs showed a weird p99 spike when the runtime picked the fallback kernel for uint8 quant. hoping this audit will surface that.
leah: can you attach the sampling proportions? we should match token length distribution and user session interarrival times from prod
sam: attaching config snippet:

```
# replay config
sampling: stratified
cohorts: mirror-cohorts-v3.json
seed: 42
kv_warmup: true
preserve_token_dist: true
repeat_ratio: 1.0
```

diego: CI harness will ramp to 500 qps and then steady 200 qps for 30m. synthetic traffic runs will mirror the same qps profile.
ci-bot: started replay job 2008501234-01 on cluster-replay-3
ci-bot: logs: "replay: loading 12k traces, anonymizing (sha256), applying cohort sampling"
maya: important: anonymizer should drop user-agent and ip fields before hashing. last time we hashed ips raw and had a privacy flag raised.
sam: confirmed, anonymizer v2 drops ip/ua -> hashes session_id only
alex: first small run results (10m window):
- replay: throughput 195 qps
- synthetic: throughput 198 qps
- replay p99 latency: 312ms
- synthetic p99 latency: 285ms
- kernel breakdown: default-attn: 60%, fused-attn-opt: 40% (but fused had 20% higher tail)
leah: that tail for fused-attn-opt is worrying. do we have kernel selection logs to see why it picked fused in those requests?
diego: yes, runtime logs (excerpt):

```
[12:14:02] request=abc123 seq_len=1024 selected_kernel=fused-attn-opt reason=kernel_perf_estimate
[12:14:02] request=abc124 seq_len=1024 selected_kernel=fused-attn-opt reason=kernel_perf_estimate
[12:14:03] request=abc125 seq_len=64 selected_kernel=default-attn reason=min_latency
```

alex: looks like the estimator chose fused for longer sequences but its performance regressed under certain batch compositions -> probably KV cache warmup interplay
sam: can we reproduce deterministically with a targeted micro-run? e.g., only seq_len 1024 cohort, 1-request batching, warm cache vs cold cache
maya: run created: replay-micro-1024-warm and replay-micro-1024-cold
ci-bot: micro-run replay-micro-1024-warm started (seed=42, qps=20, duration=10m)
ci-bot: micro-run replay-micro-1024-cold started (seed=42, kv_warmup=false)
leah: profiling hooks enabled. collect perf counters: kernel_ms, cpu_ms, memcpy_ms, kv_hit_ratio
sam: early micro-run observation: fused-attn-opt kernel_ms increased by ~35% when batch had mixed seq_len 1024+64 vs homogeneous 1024. suggests batching heuristic mis-grouping
diego: hypothesis: continuous batching groups small + large sequences when bursty, the kernel's internal workspace reallocations are causing memcpy overhead
alex: perf snippet from perf aggregator:

```
run: replay-micro-1024-warm
kernel=fused-attn-opt kernel_ms=6.5 memcpy_ms=1.4 kv_hit_ratio=0.87 batch_size=4 seq_lens=[1024,1024,64,1024]
kernel=default-attn kernel_ms=4.1 memcpy_ms=0.3 kv_hit_ratio=0.90 batch_size=4 seq_lens=[64,64,64,64]
```

maya: that's pretty telling. default kernel stays stable; fused suffers when batches are mixed-length.
sam: action items:
1) add a batching heuristic tweak to prefer homogeneous seq_len grouping for >512 tokens
2) add a kernel-safety fallback if memcpy_ms > X or observed kernel_ms jumps > 20% over baseline
3) run full apples-to-apples suite (mirror + synthetic) after patches
leah: also add a KV warmup guard: avoid evicting hot KV pages during high qps transient
diego: I'll prototype batching heuristic change and run canary against replay-mirror tomorrow morning
ci-bot: queued job 2008501234-02 (canary-batching-proto) on cluster-replay-3
deploy-bot: canary started: canary=canary-142 patch=batching-heuristic-homog
alex: quick parity check plan: compare token-by-token logits sample on 1k deterministic traces (seeded) and report divergence rate. keep threshold <= 0.2% for kernel swap paths
maya: we should also compare cost per token and p50/p95/p99 latencies across both replay and synthetic for fairness
sam: agreed. I'll document the methodology and exact metrics in the perf doc and attach the run ids
leah: one more ask: include end-to-end tail SLO impact (user-facing request completion) not just kernel_ms
sam: noted. will include SLO simulated error budget burn projection
maya: thanks — this is moving in a good direction. ping me if you need additional tracing spans
alex: postmortem-if-failed: roll back kernel selection to conservative defaults and re-run replay
sam: thanks team. I'll post the summary + links when the canary finishes. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary finished: success=false, observed p99 increase +12% on replay-mirror vs baseline
ci-bot: archived logs -> s3://replay-logs/2008501234/canary-batching-proto
leah: ok, rollback & iterate on memcpy mitigation. assigning diego + alex to follow up
sam: assigning action owners: diego (batching heuristic), alex (kernel fallback), maya (parity tests + metrics), leah (SLO impact)
maya: ack
alex: ack
diego: ack
sam: closing thread for now, will re-open with new canary results.
